'''Frederick Douglass Haynes III''' (born 1960)<ref>{{cite web|last=Lacy|first=Akela|url=https://theintercept.com/2026/02/04/texas-jasmine-crockett-house-primary-frederick-haynes/|title=He’s Running to Fill Jasmine Crockett’s House Seat From Her Left. He’s Also Her Pastor.|work=[[The Intercept]]|date=February 4, 2026|accessdate=February 7, 2026}}</ref> is an American pastor and politician from Texas. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], he is the pastor for [[Friendship-West Baptist Church]] in [[Dallas]]. He is the member-elect for [[Texas's 30th congressional district]] in the [[United States House of Representatives]].

==Early life and education==
Haynes was born in [[Dallas]]. His father, Frederick Haynes Jr., moved the family to [[San Francisco]], where Frederick Haynes Sr. was pastor at [[Third Baptist Church (San Francisco)|Third Baptist Church]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Roeback|first=Tacuma|title=Meet Rev. Frederick Haynes III: Jesse Jackson's Rainbow PUSH Successor|website=Chicago Defender|date=July 16, 2023|url=https://chicagodefender.com/meet-rev-frederick-haynes-iii-jesse-jacksons-rainbow-push-successor/|access-date=January 23, 2026}}</ref>

Haynes earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] from [[Bishop College]], a [[Master of Divinity]] from [[Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary]], and a [[Doctor of Ministry]] from the [[Graduate Theological Foundation]]. As part of his doctoral studies, he studied at [[Christ Church, Oxford|Christ Church]] at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Foster|first=Lena|title=Dr. Frederick D. Haynes, III named successor to Rev. Jesse Jackson as President and CEO of Rainbow PUSH Coalition|website=Dallas Weekly|date=July 16, 2023|url=https://dallasweekly.com/2023/07/dr-frederick-d-haynes-iii-named-successor-to-rev-jesse-jackson-as-president-and-ceo-of-rainbow-push-coalition/|access-date=January 23, 2026}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1983, Haynes became the senior pastor of [[Friendship-West Baptist Church]] in Dallas, growing its membership from 100 to over 13,000. In September 2025, he took a medical leave of absence to undergo surgery<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wfaa.com/article/news/local/frederick-haynes-senior-pastor-of-friendship-west-baptist-church-leave-of-absence-diagnosis/287-08ef6518-7787-4b1f-8c18-483fbd5d4e24|title=Frederick Haynes III, senior pastor of Friendship-West Baptist church, announces leave of absence citing medical diagnosis|date=September 14, 2025|website=WFAA|accessdate=December 9, 2025|last=Behrndt|first=Rachel}}</ref> and returned the following month.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wfaa.com/article/news/local/frederick-freddie-haynes-iii-senior-pastor-of-friendship-west-baptist-church-returns-after-medical-leave/287-d4a45422-aba6-40e8-99b5-68bb0e1f8210|title=Frederick Haynes III, senior pastor of Friendship-West Baptist church, returns to the pulpit after medical leave|date=October 18, 2025|website=WFAA|accessdate=December 9, 2025|last=Sawyers|first=Ben}}</ref> 

In 2023, Haynes succeeded [[Jesse Jackson]] as the [[chief executive officer]] of the [[Rainbow/PUSH]] Coalition.<ref>{{cite web |last=Corley |first=Cheryl |title=After more than five decades, Rev. Jesse Jackson steps down at Rainbow-Push Coalition |website=NPR |date=July 17, 2023 |url=https://www.npr.org/2023/07/17/1188183475/after-more-than-five-decades-rev-jesse-jackson-steps-down-at-rainbow-push-coalit |access-date=January 23, 2026}}</ref> Haynes stepped down from the position three months later.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/why-did-rev-haynes-step-down-from-rainbow-push/ |title=Why did Rev. Haynes step down from Rainbow PUSH? "He did not have authority to do the job," host argues. |date=April 18, 2024 |website=CBS Chicago |accessdate=December 9, 2025 |last=Dodge |first=John}}</ref>

After incumbent [[Jasmine Crockett]] announced that she would run for the [[U.S. Senate]] in the [[2026 United States Senate election in Texas|2026 election]], Haynes announced that he would [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas#District 30|run to succeed her]] in the [[U.S. House of Representatives]] for {{ushr|TX|30}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/2025/12/08/friendship-west-baptist-church-frederick-haynes-dallas-texas-congress/|title=Friendship-West Baptist Church pastor Frederick Haynes III mounts campaign for Congress|first=Gromer |last=Jeffers Jr|date=December 8, 2025|website=Dallas News|accessdate=December 9, 2025}}</ref> He was endorsed by Crockett to succeed her, as well as by state representative [[Chris Turner (Texas politician)|Chris Turner]], [[Tarrant County]] Commissioner [[Alisa Simmons]] and by Kirk Johnson, the son of Crockett's predecessor, the late Rep. [[Eddie Bernice Johnson]]. Kirk Johnson said at Haynes' launch event that Haynes was like an adopted son to his mother, and she would have encouraged voters to support him.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Birenbaum |first1=Gabby |title=Jasmine Crockett’s pastor, Frederick Haynes III, sees Congress as stage to pursue social justice |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/01/15/frederick-haynes-congress-dallas-pastor-jasmine-crockett-2026/ |access-date=February 7, 2026 |publisher= |date=January 15, 2026|work=[[Texas Tribune]]}}</ref> Haynes' campaign has also been endorsed by [[Justice Democrats]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lacy |first1=Akela |title=He's Running to Fill Jasmine Crockett's House Seat From Her Left. He's Also Her Pastor |url=https://theintercept.com/2026/02/04/texas-jasmine-crockett-house-primary-frederick-haynes/ |access-date=February 7, 2026 |publisher=|date=February 4, 2026|work=[[The Intercept]]|url-access=registration}}</ref> and the Texas [[AFL-CIO]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Texas AFL-CIO COPE Announces 2026 Primary Election Endorsements |url=https://texasaflcio.org/news/texas-afl-cio-cope-announces-2026-primary-election-endorsements |access-date=January 25, 2026}}</ref>

On March 3, 2026, Haynes won the Democratic primary for the 30th congressional district, defeating former state representative [[Barbara Mallory Caraway]] and pastor Rodney LaBruce.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 3, 2026 |title=Rev. Frederick Haynes wins Democratic primary for Texas' 30th Congressional District |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/results-texas-democratic-primary-district-30-frederick-haynes/ |access-date=March 4, 2026 |website=CBS Texas |language=en-US|last=Rosenbaum|first=Steven|last2=Candido|first2=Sergio}}</ref> Haynes won the general election on November 3.<ref>https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6134961-haynes-wins-texas-house-election/</ref>
